body_md:
# Thesis consistency and coherence

Automates the review that keeps 100+ pages of thesis prose internally
consistent and coherent, speaking to a software engineering leader, free of
filler repetition, aligned to the ESGCI rubric, and honest about
reproducibility promises.

## When to run

* Before each submission (A02, A03, A04, A05, A06).
* After any material rewrite (new section, restructure, comment resolution
  batch).
* When onboarding a new chapter into the corpus so the canonical YAMLs get
  refreshed against the newest evidence.

## Prerequisites

* `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` with the deps declared in `pyproject.toml`
  (`python-docx`, `pyyaml`, `streamlit`, `pandas`, `plotly`, `pywin32`).
* Access to `G:\My Drive\ESGCIDBA\Thesis\thesis-chapter-drafts\`.
* An initialised `thesis_analytics.db` at
  `G:\My Drive\ESGCIDBA\Thesis\thesis_analytics.db` with the citation-analytics
  tables. This skill adds `cc_` tables to the same file.
* Read `CLAUDE.md`, this skill's SKILL.md, the citation-analytics SKILL.md,
  and the four canonical YAMLs under `knowledge/`.

## Catalogue of criteria

Fifteen criteria in six tracks. Each check emits rows into `cc_findings`
with a severity in `{error, warning, info}` and a `finding_hash` that stays
stable across re-runs when the underlying content is unchanged.

### Track A — Consistency (same concept, same words)

* **A1 Terminology and definitions.** Every defined term (`review tax`,
  `correctness wedge`, `maintainer capacity restoration`, `governed
  downstream review workflow`, `corporate-sponsored open-source repository`,
  `agentic workflow`, and so on) is used with the same operational meaning
  everywhere. Canonical definitions live in `knowledge/canonical_terms.yaml`.
* **A2 Hypothesis restatement.** H1, H2, H3 as stated in `ch1 §Research
  Questions and Objectives`, `ch2 §2.9`, `ch3 §3.1`, and every downstream
  restatement mean the same thing. Canonical statements live in
  `knowledge/canonical_hypotheses.yaml`.
* **A3 Load-bearing numerical claims.** Percentages, effect sizes, sample-
  size thresholds, and named-study numbers are quoted consistently
  wherever the same claim appears. Canonical set lives in
  `knowledge/canonical_claims.yaml`.
* **A4 Straw-man citation coverage.** Every dismissive claim (a "we do not
  use survey data because ...", a "we reject synthetic control on the
  grounds that ...") is backed by at least one citation, not asserted on
  the writer's authority.

### Track B — Coherence (structural)

* **B1 Chapter-to-chapter handoffs.** Constructs introduced in ch2 are
  operationalised in ch3; data sources named in prose are catalogued in
  section 3.6; method anchors named in narrative are referenced in section
  3.7. No orphans in either direction.
* **B2 Source and method-anchor coverage.** Every data source mentioned in
  prose has a subsection in 3.6; every method anchor cited is in the
  References DOCX (checked via `v_reference_report` in the shared DB).
* **B3 Argumentative flow.** Each section's opening paragraph orients the
  reader in the chapter's argument. Missing or generic openers get flagged.
* **B4 Methodological grounding.** Every methodological choice in ch3 is
  traceable back to a ch2 finding, a gap identified in ch2, or an explicit
  amendment-memo directive. Uncited choices are the top viva risk.

### Track C — Managerial resonance (this is a DBA)

* **C1 Executive orientation of openers.** Ch1 §Background and each
  chapter's opening subsection is readable by a VP of Engineering (see
  `knowledge/canonical_persona.yaml`) without prior methodology training.
* **C2 Decision-rule coverage.** Every hypothesis outcome and wedge
  threshold links to a stated executive decision (the 3.8 matrix, a
  managerial recommendation, or a next-action pointer).
* **C3 Business-definition-before-operational-definition ordering.** For
  each construct, the business-level definition precedes the operational
  definition in reading order. A VP wants to know what a review tax IS
  before being told how it is measured.

### Track D — Editorial economy

* **D1 Verbatim and near-verbatim repetition.** Text spans of 20 or more
  words appearing in more than one section, and sentences with 80 percent
  or higher lexical overlap. Each cluster is adjudicated as `filler`
  (drop the redundant copies), `boilerplate-to-consolidate` (lift to a
  single canonical location, replace with cross-references), or
  `legitimate` (APA verbatim quote or a genuine cross-chapter recap).
* **D2 Conceptual repetition without benefit.** Same underlying idea
  restated across sections in different words. Each cluster is adjudicated
  as `serves-continuity` (helpful), `filler` (waste), or
  `boilerplate-to-consolidate` (a section-level pattern like the "execution
  results defer to Chapter 4" disclaimer that belongs in the chapter
  intro).

### Track E — Rubric compliance (ESGCI grading)

* **E1 Rubric-item coverage per assignment.** For the active assignment
  (A02, A03, A04, ...), every rubric-required component from
  `Uni_Guidelines/` is traceable to at least one section. Missing
  components are errors. Page-count guidance is reported as info only,
  since the supervisor tolerates modest deviation.

### Track F — Reproducibility register (audit trail, not a nag)

* **F1 Reproducibility promise register.** Every "we will pre-register X"
  or "we will release Y" phrase across the corpus is captured as an
  info-only finding. Not surfaced in the dashboard by default. Available
  as a filter or a dedicated register view when needed.

## Artefacts

### Canonical YAMLs (seeded once, refined over time)

Under `.github/skills/thesis-consistency-coherence/knowledge/`:

* `canonical_persona.yaml` — the VP-of-Engineering reader persona used by
  Track C. Fixed at design time.
* `canonical_hypotheses.yaml` — H1, H2, H3 canonical statements, primary
  outcome variables, theory anchors, and their managerial implications.
* `canonical_terms.yaml` — glossary of every defined construct with
  canonical prose, allowed variants, and a business-level definition
  alongside the operational one.
* `canonical_claims.yaml` — load-bearing numerical claims tied to specific
  studies, with the source citation and any allowed paraphrases.

The YAMLs are the source of truth. Every drift the checker flags is
measured against them. Edit them here to move the goalposts.

### Database

Adds `cc_` tables and `v_cc_*` views to the existing
`G:\My Drive\ESGCIDBA\Thesis\thesis_analytics.db`:

* `cc_criteria` — the fifteen-criterion catalogue as reference data.
* `cc_runs` — one row per invocation of the skill.
* `cc_findings` — one row per detected finding, with a stable
  `finding_hash` so decisions survive re-runs.
* `cc_decisions` — reviewer decisions (accept / reject / defer / discuss),
  free-text comments, and implementation status.
* `v_cc_latest` — findings from the most recent run, joined with any
  decision already left.
* `v_cc_diff_last_two` — findings that appeared, disappeared, or changed
  severity between the latest two runs.
* `v_cc_severity_rollup` — track and criterion counts per run.

Schema DDL is in `sql/consistency_schema.sql`. Idempotent: safe to run
multiple times.

### Decisions log (long-term audit)

After each implementation commit, `scripts/export_decisions.py` writes
`.github/skills/thesis-consistency-coherence/decisions_log.jsonl`. Every
row is a JSON object per decision. Text-diffable, git-tracked, survives
Google Drive's 30-day version retention for the DB itself.

### Scripts

Under `scripts/`:

* `seed_canonicals.py` — bootstrap the four YAMLs from ch1, ch2, and the
  amendment memo. Run once. Output is drafts that the candidate reviews
  and edits before use.
* `check_terms.py`, `check_hypotheses.py`, `check_claims.py`,
  `check_strawman.py` — Track A checks (A1-A4).
* `check_handoffs.py`, `check_coverage.py`, `check_flow.py`,
  `check_grounding.py` — Track B checks (B1-B4).
* `check_openers.py`, `check_decisions.py`, `check_ordering.py` — Track C
  checks (C1-C3).
* `check_repetition_verbatim.py`, `check_repetition_conceptual.py` — Track D.
* `check_rubric.py` — Track E.
* `check_promises.py` — Track F.
* `run_all.py` — orchestrator. Applies the schema (idempotent), starts a
  new `cc_runs` row, invokes every check with the run_id, prints the
  severity roll-up.
* `export_decisions.py` — dumps `cc_decisions` to `decisions_log.jsonl`.
* `implement_accepted.py` — reads `cc_decisions` where
  `decision = 'accept' AND implemented_at IS NULL`, applies the fixes to
  the DOCX files, updates `implemented_at` and the commit SHA. Runs only
  after the candidate approves in the dashboard.
* Dashboard tab code lives inside the citation-analytics
  `scripts/dashboard.py` (fourth tab, "Consistency & Coherence") so the
  candidate has one dashboard, not two.

## Pipeline

### Step 1 — Rebuild the citation-analytics DB first

The skill's coverage checks depend on the citations DB view. Rebuild it
if the DOCX corpus has changed:

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" ".github\skills\citation-analytics\scripts\build_db.py"
```

### Step 2 — Run all fifteen checks

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" ".github\skills\thesis-consistency-coherence\scripts\run_all.py"
```

Programmatic candidates land in `cc_findings` with `llm_verdict = NULL`.
The script prints the severity roll-up per track.

### Step 3 — LLM adjudication

Invoke this skill in chat and I will:

1. Read every pending candidate (`llm_verdict IS NULL`) from `cc_findings`.
2. Adjudicate each, filling in `llm_verdict` and `llm_rationale`.
3. Print a compact summary of the results.

### Step 4 — Review and decide

Launch the dashboard and open the Consistency & Coherence tab:

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" -m streamlit run ".github\skills\citation-analytics\scripts\dashboard.py"
```

Filter by track, criterion, severity, or file. Per-row inputs:
`Accept fix` / `Reject (false positive)` / `Defer` / `Needs discussion`,
plus a free-text comment. Save writes to `cc_decisions`.

### Step 5 — Implement accepted decisions

Invoke this skill in chat. I will:

1. Read `cc_decisions` where `decision = 'accept' AND implemented_at IS NULL`.
2. Group decisions logically (all A1 findings on the same term, all D1
   findings on the same boilerplate span, and so on) so each edit hits
   the right sections in one pass.
3. Apply the DOCX edits, resolve any newly-introduced style-check hits,
   commit, and update `implemented_at` and `implementation_commit`.
4. Export the `cc_decisions` rows to `decisions_log.jsonl` and commit that
   too.

## Conventions

* Everything the skill needs lives under this folder plus the shared
  `thesis_analytics.db`. No `.tmp/` scratch scripts.
* Findings survive re-runs via `finding_hash`. Never edit
  `cc_findings.hash` by hand.
* Decisions are attached to `finding_hash`, not to a specific run_id, so
  they survive re-runs.
* The canonical YAMLs are the source of truth for A1, A2, A3, C1, C3. To
  extend a check, edit the YAML, not the script.
* The dashboard is read-write for decisions and comments only.
  Everything else is read-only.

## Attribution

Governed by CLAUDE.md `§7` workflow expectations. The Track E rubric
source is `Uni_Guidelines/`. The Track B2 coverage check depends on the
citation-analytics `v_reference_report` view; if that view changes the
grounding logic here needs a revisit.
